note: Agents with a new mechanism, target or modality that are not yet approved for this disease in the US or EU, selected from peer-reviewed early-phase trials and major meetings. Early response rates often fall with more patients and longer follow-up; meeting data are not peer-reviewed.
scope: Most new CLL drugs are tested first in relapsed disease, so this list covers both untreated and relapsed CLL.

items.why: Degrading BTK, rather than blocking it, can work against the mutations that cause resistance to covalent and noncovalent BTK inhibitors, the main unmet need after a BTK inhibitor and venetoclax.
items.data: BGB-16673 (CaDAnCe-101; 68 patients with relapsed CLL/SLL): ORR 85.3% overall and 75.0% after both a BTK and a BCL2 inhibitor; 18-month PFS 65.9% at a median follow-up of 19.8 months. Bexobrutideg (NX-5948; phase 1a, 47 evaluable patients, EHA 2025): ORR 80.9% at a median follow-up of 9.0 months.
items.safety: BGB-16673: most common adverse events were fatigue (36.8%) and contusion (30.9%).
items.next: Phase 3 trials in relapsed CLL against pirtobrutinib: BGB-16673 (NCT06973187) and bexobrutideg (NCT07516093); BGB-16673 against investigator's choice (CaDAnCe-302, NCT06846671).
src: Sharma P, J Hematol Oncol 2026 (ASH 2025 summary)

items.why: A next-generation BCL2 inhibitor, more selective and potent than venetoclax in laboratory studies, with a short half-life and no accumulation. It is developed mainly with zanubrutinib as a fixed-duration first-line regimen. Conditionally approved in China (January 6, 2026) for CLL/SLL after a BTK inhibitor; not approved for CLL in the US or EU.
items.data: BGB-11417-101: 112 patients with untreated CLL/SLL received zanubrutinib with sonrotoclax 160 mg (51) or 320 mg (61); ORR 100% among patients assessed at week 48, with high rates of undetectable MRD.
items.safety: One patient stopped the combination for an adverse event; no deaths (data cutoff May 2024).
items.next: Phase 3 in untreated CLL, with zanubrutinib: vs venetoclax-obinutuzumab (BGB-11417-301, NCT06073821), vs venetoclax-acalabrutinib (BGB-11417-304, NCT07277231) and vs continuous zanubrutinib in older patients (A042302, NCT07321652).

items.why: A BCL2 inhibitor with a daily dose ramp-up over 5 to 7 days, shorter than the weekly ramp-up of venetoclax. Approved in China (July 10, 2025) for CLL/SLL after a BTK inhibitor; not approved in the US or EU.
items.data: 176 patients (154 relapsed or refractory, 22 untreated): ORR 67.4% with lisaftoclax alone (43 patients), 84.6% with rituximab (39) and 97.7% with acalabrutinib (87); among 14 patients previously given venetoclax, ORR 92.9% with lisaftoclax-acalabrutinib.
items.safety: Tumor lysis syndrome in 5 patients (2.8%; 2 clinical); grade 3 or higher neutropenia 30.1%; no treatment-related discontinuations or deaths.
items.next: Phase 3 with acalabrutinib vs chemoimmunotherapy in untreated CLL (NCT06319456) and a global phase 3 in previously treated CLL (NCT06104566).

items.why: A second noncovalent BTK inhibitor after pirtobrutinib, now in phase 3 against covalent BTK inhibitors in untreated CLL.
items.data: 47 treated patients with relapsed B-cell malignancies after at least 2 therapies (29 with CLL): ORR 75% in CLL at the recommended dose of 65 mg daily.
items.safety: Most common grade 3 or higher events: neutropenia (23.4%), febrile neutropenia (14.9%) and pneumonia (14.9%).
items.next: Phase 3: vs ibrutinib or acalabrutinib in untreated CLL (BELLWAVE-011, NCT06136559); vs chemoimmunotherapy in untreated CLL (NCT05624554); with venetoclax vs venetoclax-rituximab in relapsed CLL (NCT05947851).

items.why: T-cell-engaging antibodies are established in lymphoma. In CLL, T-cell dysfunction and cytokine release have been the obstacles, and this is a test of the approach after BTK and BCL2 inhibitors.
items.data: EPCORE CLL-1 expansion cohort: 23 heavily pretreated patients, median follow-up 22.8 months; ORR 61% and complete response 39% (67% and 43% of the 21 response-evaluable patients).
items.safety: Cytokine release syndrome in 96% (grade 3 in 17%); ICANS in 13%, all grade 1 or 2.
items.next: Phase 1b/2 continuing with optimized step-up dosing and combinations; no phase 3 in CLL identified. Another bispecific antibody, surovatamig (CD19 × CD3), is in a phase 3 consolidation trial after first-line therapy (SOUNDTRACK-C1, NCT07509151).
